name: Hotel Gabrielli Venezia, StarHotels
positioning: Historic hotel of seven palazzos on Venice's Riva degli Schiavoni, held by the Perkhofer family for five generations
best_for: Travelers who want a lagoon-front base a few steps from Piazza San Marco
Guests drawn to Venetian craftsmanship and literary history

facts.text: The hotel overlooks the Riva degli Schiavoni, a few steps from Piazza San Marco, the Biennale Gardens and the Arsenale.
The hotel is made up of seven palazzos, three of which directly face the canal.
The noble Gabrielli family were the original stewards of the 14th-century palazzo.
The hotel has been held by the Perkhofer family for five generations.
The interiors were designed by Andrea Auletta.
Rooms and suites use materials such as walnut wood and Italian marble, with golden details.
The spa features a large hot tub, a hammam, a sauna and a multi-sensory shower.
Breakfast is held in the Corte Grande, a former outdoor courtyard brought inside with a glass ceiling.
The Felice al Gabrielli restaurant is helmed by Mirko Pistorello, who sources fresh regional ingredients from the lagoon and its surroundings.
K Lounge Bar is named after Kafka, and its cocktails reference Venetian urban legends.
The hotel's Craft Experiences include a visit to an authentic Murano glass factory at Berengo Studio.
The Arsenale vaporetto stop is right outside the hotel.

highlights.text: The panoramic rooftop terrace on the sixth floor has a view of Venice stretching from the Lido to the Dogana.
The Presidential Suite has a private terrace with views of the Lagoon, San Giorgio Maggiore and the Campanile of St. Mark's.
The hotel has a 600-square-meter private garden and a private dock.
Past guests included Sigmund Freud, Adolf Loos and Franz Kafka.
The hotel's original chandeliers have been restored by Seguso and Pauly & C, family-owned studios of Murano.

considerations.text: The spa is available to all guests from Tuesday through Sunday, and advance reservation is required.
WhataHotel notes there is no on-site parking; travel is by foot or water taxi.
WhataHotel notes heavy tourist foot traffic along the waterfront promenade in high season.
